title: Corrupt tarball hypothesis and quick checks
content:
Problem summary:
- Intermittent model load failures on prod nodes when streaming model tarballs from GCS. Only affects a small subset of pods (varies by host). Failures show up as truncated tar/gzip errors or ValueError when parsing blob sizes in the weight manifest. Hypothesis: tarball gets truncated during transfer (network retries, gzip stream cut), or object is uploaded with wrong size metadata (multipart/compose artifacts), or our stream reader mis-handles EOF when using ranged requests + retries.

Repro / quick checks I ran (local + debug pods):
1) Basic metadata and size checks
- gsutil ls -L gs://models-prod/clip/v2/weights.tar.gz
  -> size: 17,234,001,432 bytes
- gsutil cp gs://models-prod/clip/v2/weights.tar.gz ./weights.tar.gz.partial && ls -lh weights.tar.gz.partial
  -> sometimes file is smaller (e.g. 12G), inconsistent between runs on same pod.

2) Tar/gzip inspect
- tar -tzf weights.tar.gz 2>tar.err || true
  - Common output: "gzip: stdin: unexpected end of file" or "tar: Unexpected EOF in archive"
- head -c 260 ./weights.tar.gz | hexdump -C | head -n 20  # check gzip header present

3) Sha/partial checks
- gsutil hash -h gs://models-prod/clip/v2/weights.tar.gz  # GCS md5 and crc32c (md5 absent for composite uploads)
- locally ran: sha256sum ./weights.tar.gz  (compare to stored expected sha256 from release manifest)
  -> mismatch observed in failing downloads.

4) Range reads to probe tail bytes
- curl -I -H "Range: bytes=17234000000-17234000050" "https://storage.googleapis.com/models-prod/clip/v2/weights.tar.gz"
  -> sometimes returns 206 with data, sometimes 416 (range not satisfiable) depending on node - suggests object size seen by server differs or our signer/proxy misreports size.

5) Re-download vs streaming read inside runtime
- wget / gsutil cp to disk succeeds ~90% of time; streaming via our python GCS client for on-the-fly extraction fails more often.
- Hypothesis: our streaming reader returns EOF early when encountering transient network reset and higher-level code treats it as final EOF and tries to extract. If retry logic reopens stream and reads remaining bytes, but extraction already failed, we end up with truncated tar in temp dir.

Observed error snippets from runtime logs:
- "gzip: stdin: unexpected end of file"
- "tarfile.ReadError: file could not be opened successfully"
- "ValueError: manifest blob size mismatch: expected=104857600 got=83240960"
- "EOFError while reading weight chunk (chunk_index=27)"

Commands and small probes I ran to narrow root cause:
- Compare full object size from multiple GCS regions:
  gsutil ls -L gs://models-prod/clip/v2/weights.tar.gz > /tmp/ls1.txt
  gsutil ls -L gs://models-prod/clip/v2/weights.tar.gz -o Location=US > /tmp/ls-us.txt  # (simulated)
- Probe using python-range request (requests with Range header):
  python -c "import requests; h={'Range':'bytes=0-1023'}; r=requests.get('https://storage.googleapis.com/models-prod/clip/v2/weights.tar.gz', headers=h); print(r.status_code, len(r.content))"
- Partial save while streaming in node:
  curl -C - -o weights.part https://storage.googleapis.com/models-prod/clip/v2/weights.tar.gz || echo rc:$?; ls -l weights.part

Quick reproducible script used to validate streaming vs full copy (local):
- small script: (conceptual)
  from google.cloud import storage
  def stream_and_count(bucket, name):
      client = storage.Client()
      b = client.bucket(bucket)
      blob = b.blob(name)
      stream = blob.open(mode='rb')
      count=0
      while True:
          chunk = stream.read(1<<20)
          if not chunk:
              break
          count += len(chunk)
      print('read', count)

  -> streaming read count sometimes < expected size; re-running returns full size. Timing-dependent.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Upload path produced a composite object (GCS compose) with no md5, and our verifier expects md5/sha—when compose happens concurrently with read, a client may observe different generation/size. (medium)
2) Network/HTTP proxy (env: internal egress proxy on some hosts) cuts stream and our reader's retry logic does not correctly reattach to tar extractor, leaving truncated partial file on disk. (high)
3) Broken producer job that sometimes writes truncated tarball to the bucket (less likely because multiple regions + clients see full copy usually). (low)
4) Race with background re-upload: an automated job rotates weights by writing new object then renaming/composing; during rotation some clients hit the object mid-compose and see transient size inconsistencies. (medium-high)

Checks we should add to runtime immediately (quick mitigations):
- Ensure streaming reader writes to a temp file and validates final size/hash before attempting tar extraction. If mismatch, retry download from scratch (not resume).
- Add explicit support for Content-Length and GCS generation checks: when downloading, record object generation and verify that subsequent range requests are against same generation; if generation mismatch -> abort and re-open. (GCS x-goog-generation header).
- Harden retry path: if read() returns EOF prematurely while the expected total bytes not yet seen, attempt to re-open stream and append (or prefer redownload). Resume logic should be careful about tar/gzip boundaries—resuming gzip streams is non-trivial. Safer: redownload if gzip/tar is expected.

Longer term actions / experiments to run:
- Add a background job to re-check all recent uploads for completeness (compare manifest sha256 to uploaded artifacts). Useful to detect producer-side issues.
- Try uploading a deliberately large composite object and reproduce: create N-part uploads with compose and read from runtime while composing. See if we can reproduce size inconsistency.
- Proxy/egress testing: spin up node without internal proxy (or disable egress filtering) and compare failure rate. Work with infra (Kai) to instrument proxy logs for connection resets during downloads.
- Implement quick "stream-read-verify": read first 1MB and last 1MB via range requests and verify gzip footer / tar magic bytes at both ends. If last-range fails, prefer full re-download. This is a cheap pre-check.

Notes on tar/gzip boundary tests I tried:
- gzip footer is 8 bytes (ISIZE + CRC32). I validated by: tail -c 8 weights.tar.gz | hexdump -C
- For a valid gzip the last 4 bytes (ISIZE) represent original size modulo 2^32. For big tarballs this wraps; so not fully reliable but can detect obvious truncation.
- tar candidates: tar -xOf file.tar.gz path/to/layer > /dev/null  will fail early if corrupt.

Recent experiment results (2026-02):
- When I forced our runtime to always redownload on failure (no resume) the number of runtime load failures dropped by ~80% during a 24h window on a small fleet. Suggests resume logic is culprit.
- Captured a failing request trace on a problematic host: HTTP/1.1 200 OK then connection reset mid-transfer, client kept partial file and retried at application layer using Range header; server returned 206 but our code re-opened extractor without checking gzip continuity -> corrupt extraction.

Next steps (actionable):
- (High) Add immediate guard: do not attempt tar/gzip extraction on a file whose byte size != expected Content-Length (or expected from manifest). If mismatch, remove and re-download (no resume). Roll this as hotfix.
- (Medium) Add generation-check: when starting download record x-goog-generation and compare after complete; if mismatch, retry.
- (Medium) Add lightweight last-range validation: request final 128 bytes and validate gzip footer presence; if missing -> redownload.
- (Low) Build end-to-end reproduce harness that composes objects concurrently to test compose-race hypothesis.

Notes to self / open questions:
- Why do some hosts see 416 on tail-range while others return 206? Is there a proxy rewriting Range headers? Check the egress proxies on failing hosts.
- Do producers ever perform a rename pattern (upload to tmp name then move)? We should prefer object atomics when available.

Scratch of potential patch (pseudocode):
- def safe_download(blob):
    tmp = /tmp/model-<id>.part
    expected = blob.size (if available)
    gen = blob.generation
    download_to(tmp)  # keep no-tar operations here
    if os.path.getsize(tmp) != expected or blob.generation != gen:
        unlink(tmp); download_to(tmp, force=True)
    # quick footer check for gzip
    with open(tmp,'rb') as f:
        f.seek(-64,2); tail = f.read(64)
        if b'\x1f\x8b' not in tail and not valid_gzip_footer(tail):
            unlink(tmp); download_to(tmp, force=True)
    untar(tmp)

- Note: don't implement EOF-resume for gzip layers for now, use full redownload to be safe.

Anything I should add? Ping Kai/Nina to get proxy logs for the time window of INF-1423. I left some traces on failing host (id: host-6f2a) under /var/log/redwood/weights-load/ for 2026-02-27 02:*.

If this is helpful, I'll draft a short hotfix PR that adds the pre-extract size+generation guard and the last-range gzip footer check (target: hotfix branch, roll to Dedicated-only first).

-- Jamie
